details:
Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive web application that empowers anyone to investigate how Earth’s climate variables are changing at any location on the planet. By pulling 34 years of real NASA satellite measurements from the NASA POWER API (Langley Research Center), the app runs rigorous statistical analysis and delivers a clear, detective-style verdict on what is changing, how fast, and whether it is real signal or random noise.

The app directly addresses all four challenge questions: it identifies whether a variable is trending up or down using OLS linear regression, determines statistical significance using both the OLS p-value and the Mann-Kendall trend test, flags extreme anomaly years using z-score detection at the ±2σ threshold, and compares decade-by-decade averages from the 1990s through the 2020s.

Users simply enter any latitude and longitude, choose from six Earth system variables — air temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, solar radiation, or dew point temperature — and click Analyze. The app instantly fetches data from NASA POWER, computes the trend slope, R-squared value, Kendall tau, p-value, and anomaly years, then visualizes everything on an interactive trend chart with anomaly markers highlighted in red and green.

The tool requires no installation, no API key, no login, and no coding knowledge. It works in any browser and is fully open source. It was built to make NASA’s free and open Earth science data accessible to students, researchers, educators, and citizens worldwide.
